pages.text: $(1)=$() only compares. To store a value, use ASSIGN. $(1)⊕$() turns numbers and lists into text, so $(1)'a' ⊕ 1 ⊕ "b"$() gives $(1)"a1b"$().

$(1)\$() only works with INTEGERs. The result keeps the sign of the left number: $(1)-7 \ 2$() is $(1)-1$(). Dividing by zero raises DIVISION_BY_ZERO, with $(1)/$() and $(1)\$(), for FLOATs too: $(1)1.5 / 0.0$() doesn't give infinity.

TIME values can be compared with $(1)<$(), $(1)>$() and the others: the earlier time is the smaller one. $(1)⊕$() writes a TIME as ISO text in UTC with milliseconds, like $(1)2026-10-19T12:05:09.250Z$(). For the local time, use FORMAT of c0de/strings.
